enum_surface.instructions: Given intentional else fallback and the full effect-bearing comparison, which option supplies the required strict-case intent most simply without claiming reduced source or changed existing-if semantics? Advice only; retain uncertainty and missing actual runtime evidence.

criteria.informational_if: Keep ordinary if/else sources; add finite analysis/reporting for immutable enum subject equality/membership branches, identifying fallback-only, duplicate/unreachable cases without turning deliberate fallback into an error. Adds no control syntax and preserves future-case acceptance; does not provide the requested opt-in strict missing-case rejection.
criteria.strict_conditional: Add an explicit new strictness marker for a bounded if chain and analyze immutable exact enum subject equality/membership, full coverage and duplicate cases while ordinary unmarked if remains unchanged. Provides strict rejection with existing effect syntax and avoids duplicate terminal bodies; adds a public marker and conditional-shape recognition/diagnostic contract that must not overclaim arbitrary booleans.
criteria.enum_match: Add optional statement match with case single-name arms for a known nonnullable finite enum, requiring full coverage and rejecting duplicates/unknown owner cases. Ordinary if/else stays unchanged. Provides strict rejection with explicit intent and simple arm-domain analysis, but adds a new control/arm construct across parser/resolver/checker/effect/IR/emitter and can duplicate shared effects; no source-size savings claimed.

case_identity.instructions: Choose the exact case-name contract for optional match when a local parameter and two different enum owners can share a spelling; preserve ordinary expression binding behavior and expose the added concept. Conditional advice only; do not imply match is already implemented.

criteria.subject_labels: If match is selected, case-position single names are labels in the checked subject enum domain, rather than expression references; a lexical parameter with the same name does not capture a label. Require an actual subject case, canonical checked case authority and duplicate checking. Wrong-owner expressions/qualified paths/pattern forms are unsupported. Existing expression lexical precedence is unchanged. Adds a clear label position whose identity is determined by the subject.
criteria.lexical_expressions: If match is selected, resolve case names as ordinary expressions with existing lexical-before-expected-case rules; require exact subject enum identity and one compile-time known case. Same-name text or foreign-enum parameters refuse rather than being reinterpreted. Preserves expression identity precedence, but a literal-looking case can be captured by an unrelated local and may require author renaming or an additional qualified case notation.
